Jordan —

Thanks for taking this on. StrataHealth is preparing a private VPC/on‑prem deployment for PHI workloads and we need a short, actionable review of the proposed key custody and cryptographic supply‑chain. Our primary asks:

- Confirm where plaintext key material will and will not exist in the Redwood stack (we need a strong assurance you never persist customer plaintext).
- Review the BYOK import flow (KMIP/PKCS#11 or wrapped key import) and the HSM boundary for wrapping/unwrapping.
- Recommended rotation windows and automated rotation vs manual operator actions.
- Escrow/backup approach for customer keys and recovery drill cadence.
- Network restrictions and egress for the KMS/HSM control channels (we cannot have unmediated outbound egress from the key management VLAN).
- Audit log retention (we have regulatory requirement: 13 months for key ops).

I've attached our initial diagram (crypto-supplychain-diagram-v1.vsdx) and a partial questionnaire. Can the Redwood team (network + cryptography SMEs) review and mark up the diagram with recommended changes and assumptions?

Subject: Re: Cryptographic supply-chain and key custody review for StrataHealth private deployment

Quick technical notes from the design side — high level recommendations and assumptions. I'll attach a detailed keyflow sketch in the follow-up.

Assumptions
- Deployment mode: private VPC with optional on‑prem HSM island (customer-provided or vendor-managed HSM appliances).
- No requirement for Redwood to hold plaintext customer keys. All customer root keys must be wrapped by a customer-controlled wrapping key during import.

High level flow (recommended)
1) BYOK import: customer generates root key material in their environment (or an approved HSM). They wrap the key under a customer wrapping key (CWK) and upload the wrapped blob to Redwood over a mutually authenticated TLS channel. Import endpoint supports KMIP v1.4 and PKCS#11-wrapped blobs; we also support an offline import via USB-encrypted media for air-gapped installs.

2) Key custody: Redwood stores only the wrapped key blob and metadata (key id, algorithm, policy, key versioning, key lineage). The unwrapping operation happens inside an HSM boundary (either on-prem HSM appliance or cloud HSM within the customer VPC). Plaintext keying material must never be exported from the HSM.

3) Wrapping keys & escrows: two viable choices—(A) Customer-managed wrapping key (preferred) stored in customer HSM; Redwood never has access to CWK plaintext. (B) Split-key escrow (threshold N-of-M) managed jointly (customer + third party) for recovery — if StrataHealth requires automated recoveries without customer HSM presence. For (B) we recommend threshold 2-of-3 with clear custody controls and documented recovery drills.

4) Rotation policy:
- Automated rewraps for short-lived intermediate keys (e.g., weekly token keys) where HSM supports in‑place rewrap without exposing plaintext.
- Root/key material rotation windows are customer-defined; typical recommendation: annual rotation for root KEKs, with quarterly validation and quarterly automatic key versioning for operational keys.
- Rolling rotation: ensure key IDs include version timestamps and maintain at least 2 versions online to allow in-flight session recovery.

5) Operator separation and access control:
- HSM admin role (init/unseal/firmware) is separate from key ops role (create/rotate/unwrap). Human operator actions requiring unseal or maintenance must be logged and require dual-authorization.
- Use short-lived service identities (OIDC / mTLS certs) for Redwood runtime components; no long-lived plaintext credentials with direct HSM access.

6) Networking & egress constraints:
- Management plane (HSM admin) is restricted to a dedicated management VLAN accessible only from a hardened bastion host with jumpbox audit.
- KMS control channel only communicates over mTLS to authorized endpoints and does not permit arbitrary outbound HTTP(S) from the key management VLAN. Logs are forwarded to SIEM over a controlled, whitelisted syslog endpoint.

7) Auditability & retention:
- HSM produces tamper-evident operation logs; Redwood will surface these logs for key ops and administrative events. For compliance we can pipeline HSM audit entries to the customer's SIEM with configurable retention; default recommended retention is 13 months to match your regulatory ask.

8) Disaster recovery & drills:
- If escrow/backup exists, perform quarterly recovery drills on a non-production copy. Document and time-box recovery RTO/RPO per customer SLAs.

Vendor/technical notes
- Prefer FIPS 140-2/3 Level 3 HSMs for on-prem appliances handling PHI. For cloud HSM, validate provider attestation and key isolation model.
- Attestation: leverage HSM attestation for integrity checks and provide customers an attestation token post-import.

Open questions for Claire
- Do you prefer customer-only wrapping key (no escrow) or require Redwood-managed escrow (threshold)?
- Any preferred HSM vendors we should validate against?

I'll draft an annotated diagram and a concise runbook for review by 2026-10-01 EOD.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cryptographic supply-chain and key custody review for StrataHealth private deployment

Vivek — this is very helpful, thank you. A few clarifications / redlines from our side: 

- Escrow: StrataHealth policy prefers customer-only control of the root wrapping key for production PHI keys. We are open to threshold escrow for non-PHI developer/test keys, but production roots must be customer-exclusive.
- Plaintext guarantee: we need a contractual clause stating Redwood will not persist plaintext key material and that any unwrapping occurs only within an HSM we can inspect or that provides attestation. Can you confirm Redwood's standard language for this?
- Recovery drills: quarterly drills are acceptable, but we need a documented after-action report template — can Redwood own the run of the drill and supply the AAR?
- Audit retention: 13 months is a minimum. Please confirm whether Redwood can support immutable storage (WORM) for critical audit logs or whether we need to stage them in our SIEM.

I'll attach the completed portion of the questionnaire (security-questionnaire-draft.xlsx) with comments inline. Two small requests: can you add explicit network ACLs to the diagram (management VLAN, HSM VLAN, SIEM egress) and include a short note on key revocation semantics for previously issued session tokens?

Thanks — can we get the annotated diagram + runbook by EOD today per Jordan's note?

Claire
Claire Summers
Security Architect, StrataHealth
